messages:
elaine (People Ops): Hey folks — I'm putting together a tiny one-page kit managers can drop into 1:1s to help teams map quarterly work into 2x committed + 1x stretch. Wanted a quick sanity check and any micro-phrases you use for coaching. Goal is: short, copy/pasteable, and usable in 10m.

mike (Eng Manager): Love this. A single visual + 3 canned prompts would be perfect.

elaine (People Ops): Quick draft below. Thoughts? 

```
Goal framing heatmap (1p)
- Top axis: Impact (low -> high)
- Left axis: Certainty/Complexity (low -> high)

Quadrants: 
  A (High impact / Low complexity): Commit 1-2
  B (High impact / High complexity): Commit 0-1, stretch candidate
  C (Low impact / Low complexity): Nice-to-have / backlog
  D (Low impact / High complexity): Deprioritize

Commitment rule: each IC picks 2 committed items from A/B (combined) + 1 stretch from B (ambitious) or C (skill growth)

Manager micro-prompts (use in 1:1):
  - "Which of these will move a metric we both care about this quarter?"
  - "What's the smallest shippable outcome we can commit to?"
  - "If we hit a blocker, what do we deprioritize to keep momentum?"

Self-review bite-size bullets (IC):
  - Outcome: one line w/ metric or user impact
  - My contribution: 2 bullets
  - Risk/uncertainty: 1 line
  - Ask from manager: 1 line

Calibration rubric (1 line each):
  - Met: delivered outcome and metric hit
  - Partial: shipped but metric short
  - Missed: did not ship / major blocker
```

tara (ML IC): This is really usable — love the commit rule. For ML infra we often need to call out data/label cost as separate axis. Maybe add a tiny row: "resource cost (low/high)" under the heatmap.

jonas (Manager, Platform): +1 to adding resource cost. Also recommend a simple naming convention for goals so tracking works across teams: `team.goal.short` (e.g., `platform.cache.hit-rate`). Makes cross-team rollups easier.

mike (Eng Manager): One micro-edit: change "Commitment rule" wording to avoid implying a hard cap — managers should adapt for critical tasks. Maybe "target: 2 committed + 1 stretch, adjust as needed for priorities."

elaine (People Ops): Good call. I'll soften the language. Any quick examples I can paste for self-review bullets?

tara (ML IC): Example: 
- Outcome: Reduced inference p95 latency by 18% for the recommendations model (p95 420ms -> 344ms).
- My contribution: Implemented async batching and tuned kernel schedule; added e2e perf tests.
- Risk: Potential variability on 3rd-party infra during peak load.
- Ask: Help prioritize extra node hours for canary in week 8.

mike (Eng Manager): My manager-ready phrasing for calibration: 
- "Met": Outcome delivered, metric target met or exceeded.
- "On track with risk": Delivery shipped but metric is within 10% of target; additional runway suggested.
- "Shifted": Scope changed for business reason; document tradeoffs.

elaine (People Ops): This is gold — I'll iterate and post a final copy in #docs-goals and pin a short checklist in the templates doc. ETA EOD. Thanks everyone! :tada: 

sre-bot: Template created: https://redwood.internal/docs/templates/quarterly-goal-heatmap (auto-post) :white_check_mark:

mike (Eng Manager): Awesome, thanks @elaine. Will share in our manager sync tomorrow.

jonas (Manager, Platform): Can you also drop a version with a one-line manager calibration table (for skip-levels)? super helpful.

elaine (People Ops): Yep — adding skip-level table now. Will notify when updated.

mike (Eng Manager): quick nit: in the code block maybe bold the manager prompts so they're easy to copy.

elaine (People Ops): Will do. Finalizing now.
